primaryDeliverable.description: Standalone six-style art-direction prototype. Each style has five vertically stacked 16:9 ocean-depth panels. Each panel uses its matching unchanged ocean background and a transparent Codex-generated creature composition. The style dropdown replaces all five image pairs.

acceptanceEvidence.requirement: Six distinct styles, each paired with all five depth tiers
acceptanceEvidence.observed: Six dropdown choices; five 16:9 panels for every choice; all 60 background/creature image files decode and match their selected style folder.

acceptanceEvidence.requirement: Native Codex creature compositions exported as transparent overlays over existing ocean panels
acceptanceEvidence.observed: Thirty distinct native source PNGs and thirty RGBA 1600x900 transparent overlay PNGs; all source and export hashes, dimensions, and alpha bounds rechecked on disk.

acceptanceEvidence.requirement: Displayed creature families and depth groupings match the packaged 3D renderer roster
acceptanceEvidence.observed: Renderer depth curves, vector-to-creature rules, and attack records reproduce the roster; all 30 overlays were visually checked against the expected family set. Alt text now derives names from the canonical roster instead of a hard-coded per-depth list.

acceptanceEvidence.requirement: Changing style switches the complete five-depth set
acceptanceEvidence.observed: Browser dropdown changed sequentially through all six styles; each time it rendered and decoded five backgrounds and five matching creature overlays, with alt names matching the canonical roster.

acceptanceEvidence.requirement: Preserve scope: no 3D implementation, no main-app/background changes, no publication
acceptanceEvidence.observed: The prototype is additive and standalone. Existing ocean backgrounds remain unchanged. The earlier RetroDiffusion comparisons and six-family recolor/evolution study are separate; neither is counted as proof for these 30 Codex-generated style/depth layers.

laterSeparateUserRequest.relationship: Additive family-evolution study; it does not replace the primary six-style/five-depth viewer.
laterSeparateUserRequest.scope: Six families, three forms each: existing base shared by Sunlight/Twilight; one new native Midnight/Abyss form; one new native advanced Trench form. Twelve new Codex-native images and six offline recolored bases.

limitations: Creature layers are representative compositions, not 50 separately interactive species instances.
Adjacent depth panels are not seamless panorama tiles.
Codex generation quota/price was not reported.

Creature layers represent the correct renderer species families by depth, but repeated individual counts are not guaranteed in each generated illustration; the audit records one confirmed Abyss anglerfish undercount.
